newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ex-Moscow air cargo rates off but volume higher.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Moscow air cargo rates off but volume higher.

text.p: Rates for cargo operations from Russia's leading air cargo gateway -- Moscow's Sheremetyevo international airport -- have fallen over the last four weeks as the market becomes more active, freight forwarders said.
Rates to Frankfurt were five cents lower at US$1.07 per kg for a 100 kg shipment, six cents lower at $1.15 to London and six cents lower at $1.30 to Luxembourg.
Nikolai Belyayev, sales manager of EMS Garant Post, a forwarder for Air France, said the market had been very active during recent weeks.
"Rates have fallen by about ten percent. We had a lot of shipments," he said.
Nadezda Sokolova, sales manager of forwarders Aeroservice, said cargo turnover had risen 15 percent over the last 14 days.

"The market is a very active now, but the Western airlines (we deal with) are not hurrying to change their tariffs. By comparison, Aeroflot's tariffs have become cheaper than in September," Sokolova said.
She said the tariff difference between Russian and Western carriers was about 40 US cents per kg for a 100 kg shipment. "We feel the difference," she added.
Peter Vins, president of Vinlund Air, said Aeroflot's October tariffs were about 10 percent lower than in September.
"Swissair and Austrian Airlines have also lowered their tariffs," he said, adding that he expected market activity to reach a peak at the start of December.
Lilia Sirbu, managing director of Icaros International Cargo Service, said the air cargo market's prospects looked good for the rest of the year.
Alexander Buchinchik, Burlington Air Express Moscow export supervising manager, said the numbers of shipments had been growing over recent weeks.
"We see lower tariffs in the market now," he said.
Meanwhile, rates to three key U.S. destinations -- New York, Miami and San Francisco -- were down by 31 cents to $2.65, down 17 cents to $3.35 and down 36 cents to $3.24 respectively.
Buchinchik said shipments to these U.S. destinations were very stable but shipments to Europe were weaker compared to previous months.
"Routes to China and Japan had a very good load factor," he added.
Sirbu said her company was handling shipments through Air France with a rate of $1.50 per one kg on the route Moscow-Helsinki-Paris-India compared with $2.38 two months ago.

"We have a long-term contract from the Ministry of Rail Transport to deliver 1,500 kg of communication equipment a week by air from Europe to Moscow over the next 36 months. The deal has good prospects," she said.

Sokolova said her company was handling many shipments of electronic goods and metals from Sheremetyevo international airport to new destinations such as Almaty and Karaganda in Kazakhstan and Krasnoyarsk in Siberia.
"Since Transaero began regular flights new possibilities have opened up for us on these routes," she said.
A manager of Chapman Freeborn Russia said the company had sent big shipments of metals from Moscow to Estonia.

"Estonian Airlines plans to extend cargo operations between Russia and Estonia operating Boeing B-737s," said the manager, who asked to remain anonymous. She said her company was in talks with Iberia to become its cargo agent.
She also said there were stable deliveries of flowers from Amsterdam to St Petersburg. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
